title: Parsing A Boolean Expression
summary: A boolean expression evaluates to true or false.
statement: A boolean expression evaluates to true or false. It can be 't' for true, 'f' for false, '!(subExpr)' for the logical NOT of subExpr, or '&(subExpr1, subExpr2, ..., subExprn)' or '|(subExpr1, subExpr2, ..., subExprn)' for the logical AND or OR of multiple sub-expressions, respectively. Given a string expression, return its evaluated result. The expression is guaranteed to be valid and adhere to these rules.
constraints: Expressions contain t,f, unary !, and n-ary & and |.
hints: Operators remain on a stack until their closing parenthesis.
Push literals and operators, ignoring commas and opening parentheses.
At a close, pop operand literals through the operator, evaluate it, and push one literal result.
Nested subexpressions reduce before their enclosing operator, matching the grammar.
editorial: Nested subexpressions reduce before their enclosing operator, matching the grammar.

tests.explanation: Both operands of the outer OR are false.
The nested OR is false, so the enclosing AND is also false.
